facts.raw_span: A 67-year-old woman
31-year history of recurrent depressive disorder
depressed mood, anhedonia, nervousness, fatigue, decreased appetite, and poor sleep
beginning 5 months after COVID-19
two severe episodes responsive to escitalopram (up to 20 mg/d) and duloxetine (up to 60 mg/d)
intolerance to venlafaxine, bupropion, and trazodone
mother had mania
denied iron deficiency anemia, hypothyroidism, or substance abuse
Physical and neurologic examinations and routine laboratory tests were unremarkable
new deep itching and creeping sensations in her bilateral shoulders and arms
worse at rest, partially relieved by movement, and predominantly occurring in the evening
causing night-time sleep disturbance

beginning 5 months after COVID-19

concepts.why: The patient has a 31-year history of recurrent depressive disorder and is experiencing depressed mood, anhedonia, and other symptoms consistent with major depressive disorder.
The patient developed new deep itching and creeping sensations in her bilateral shoulders and arms after taking duloxetine, which is a known side effect of the medication.
The patient's mother had mania, which increases the patient's risk of developing bipolar disorder.
The patient developed depressive symptoms beginning 5 months after COVID-19, which may be related to the viral infection.
The patient developed paresthesia while taking duloxetine, which is a serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor.
The patient has a history of severe depressive episodes and has tried multiple medications, including escitalopram and duloxetine, with limited response.
The patient experienced night-time sleep disturbance while taking duloxetine, which is a known side effect of the medication.
The patient developed paresthesia while taking escitalopram, which is a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor.

rationales.F02: Long history of depressive disorder increases likelihood of Major Depressive Disorder and Treatment-Resistant Depression.
rationales.F04: Onset of depression 5 months after COVID-19 suggests Post-COVID-19 Depression.
rationales.F06: Intolerance to multiple antidepressants increases likelihood of Treatment-Resistant Depression.
rationales.F10: New deep itching and creeping sensations are indicative of paresthesia, which could be induced by duloxetine or escitalopram.
rationales.F11: Characteristics of paresthesia, such as worsening at rest and relief with movement, support the diagnosis of Duloxetine-Induced Paresthesia or Serotonin-Norepinephrine Reuptake Inhibitor-Induced Paresthesia.
